concepts.name: Problem worth solving
concepts.summary: Recognise that a venture starts from a specific, painful problem faced by identifiable people rather than from a clever idea.

concepts.name: Target customer segment
concepts.summary: Explain who the customer is and why a narrow, well-defined group is a better starting point than everyone.

concepts.name: Customer discovery interviews
concepts.summary: Understand that interviews are used to learn about customers' real behaviour and problems, not to pitch or validate your idea.

concepts.name: Value proposition
concepts.summary: State in one sentence what benefit the product gives a specific customer and why it is better than the alternatives.

concepts.name: Minimum viable product
concepts.summary: Explain that an MVP is the smallest thing that tests a key assumption and generates learning, not a poor-quality full product.

concepts.name: Business model basics
concepts.summary: Name the ways a startup earns revenue, such as subscriptions, one-off sales, ads or commissions, and what costs it must cover.

concepts.name: Founder roles and commitment
concepts.summary: Describe why founding teams need complementary skills and shared commitment, and what co-founders are responsible for.

misconceptions.text: A great idea is the most important ingredient and should be kept secret until launch.
Customer interviews are for asking people whether they like your idea.
An MVP is a low-quality, stripped-down version of the finished product.

concepts.name: Past-behaviour interview technique
concepts.summary: Conduct interviews asking about specific past events and current workarounds, avoiding hypotheticals and compliments.

concepts.name: Lean canvas
concepts.summary: Fill in a lean canvas covering problem, segment, solution, channels, revenue, costs, key metrics and unfair advantage, and mark the riskiest assumptions.

concepts.name: Problem-solution fit
concepts.summary: Judge from interview evidence whether the problem is frequent and painful enough and whether your solution addresses it.

concepts.name: Riskiest assumption testing
concepts.summary: List the assumptions behind an idea and design a cheap experiment for the one that would break the business if wrong.

concepts.name: MVP types
concepts.summary: Choose and build a suitable MVP form such as a landing page, concierge service, Wizard of Oz or prototype to test a hypothesis.

concepts.name: Pricing and unit economics basics
concepts.summary: Set an initial price and compute simple per-customer revenue and cost to see if each sale makes money.

concepts.name: Founder equity split basics
concepts.summary: Explain how founders divide ownership, why vesting with a cliff protects the team, and what the cap table records.

misconceptions.text: If friends and family say they love the idea, the problem has been validated.
A lean canvas is a finished plan that should be completed once and then followed.
Splitting equity 50/50 immediately with no vesting is fair and simple, so nothing can go wrong.

concepts.name: Synthesising interview evidence
concepts.summary: Analyse many interviews to separate patterns from anecdotes and decide what the evidence supports.

concepts.name: Validation metrics and thresholds
concepts.summary: Set success criteria in advance for experiments and tell actionable metrics from vanity metrics.

concepts.name: Customer acquisition channels
concepts.summary: Test channels such as outbound sales, content and referrals and compare how well each reaches the target segment.

concepts.name: Landing first paying customers
concepts.summary: Win initial customers through direct outreach and manual sales, using preorders or paid pilots as proof of willingness to pay.

concepts.name: CAC, LTV and payback
concepts.summary: Calculate customer acquisition cost, lifetime value and payback period and analyse whether the model can be profitable.

concepts.name: Pivot or persevere decision
concepts.summary: Analyse evidence against hypotheses to decide whether to continue, adjust a part of the model or pivot.

concepts.name: Bootstrapping versus outside funding
concepts.summary: Compare bootstrapping, angels and venture capital by control, speed, expectations and fit with the business.

concepts.name: Vesting and equity agreements
concepts.summary: Apply vesting schedules, cliffs and role-based adjustments to structure a fair founder equity agreement.

misconceptions.text: Signups, page views and compliments show the startup has traction.
Every startup should raise venture capital, and raising money is a sign of success.
A pivot means the startup has failed and starts again from nothing.

concepts.name: Product-market fit assessment
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether retention, organic demand and customer pull show real product-market fit rather than early enthusiasm.

concepts.name: Market sizing critique
concepts.summary: Analyse top-down and bottom-up market estimates and spot unrealistic claims about market size.

concepts.name: Pitch deck narrative design
concepts.summary: Judge and shape a pitch deck so that problem, solution, market, traction, team and ask form a credible story for investors.

concepts.name: Dilution and cap table modelling
concepts.summary: Model how successive rounds, option pools and convertibles dilute founders and affect their incentives.

concepts.name: Funding terms evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate valuation, dilution, SAFEs, liquidation preferences and board control to decide whether an offer is acceptable.

concepts.name: Scalable sales and channel repeatability
concepts.summary: Judge whether acquisition is repeatable beyond founder-led sales and decide when to invest in scaling it.

concepts.name: Strategic pivot types
concepts.summary: Distinguish customer, problem, channel and business-model pivots and choose the one suggested by the data.

misconceptions.text: A high valuation is always the best term in a funding offer.
A huge total addressable market proves the opportunity is attractive.
Revenue growth from founder-led sales means the company is ready to scale.

concepts.name: Opportunity selection strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate competing opportunities against founder strengths, market timing, defensibility and risk appetite to commit to one.

concepts.name: Designing a funding strategy
concepts.summary: Create a funding plan sequencing bootstrapping, grants, angels and venture rounds to match milestones and keep control.

concepts.name: Defensibility and moat creation
concepts.summary: Design sources of durable advantage such as network effects, data, brand or switching costs into the business.

concepts.name: Founder conflict and governance
concepts.summary: Evaluate governance structures and resolve founder conflicts, departures and control disputes in a way that protects the company.

concepts.name: Business model innovation
concepts.summary: Create or redesign a business model, pricing and distribution to unlock a market that existing models fail to serve.

concepts.name: Portfolio of experiments system
concepts.summary: Build a company-wide system of prioritised experiments and metrics that keeps learning fast as the company grows.

concepts.name: Exit and long-term outcomes
concepts.summary: Evaluate exit paths, including acquisition, IPO or staying independent, and how they align with investor and founder goals.

misconceptions.text: Strong execution alone makes a company defensible, so a moat is unnecessary.
Founder disputes can be settled informally later without hurting the company.
Every venture-backed company should aim for an IPO as the only successful exit.
